text:
Quick flag before you rely on that first part: it cut off mid-budget table, so the one-page moving-day checklist and several other pieces you asked for never made it. Here's the rest, plus two fixes.

**Corrections to the earlier draft**
- **Emissions testing:** Oregon DEQ testing applies in the **Portland metro** and **Rogue Valley (Medford)** areas. I wrongly included Klamath Falls. Check DEQ's current map once you know your address.
- **Landlord notice:** I listed it in both Phase 1 and Phase 3. Send **one written notice now** (Phase 1), then use Phase 3 to confirm the move-out inspection and deposit-return address.
- **Timing:** Your move lands in mid-July, peak moving season. Book movers, trucks, and vehicle shippers this week or next, not at the 2-month mark.

---

## Budget Table (completed)

| Item | Estimate | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Contingency fund | 10–15% of total | Don't skip this |

**Rough "getting everything there" totals** (excludes rent and deposits; summer pricing pushes toward the high end):

| Scenario | Ballpark |
|---|---|
| DIY truck, one drives truck, one drives car and dog | $2,900–$5,800 |
| Portable container + drive car | $3,500–$6,500 |
| Hybrid (you pack, movers load/drive) + drive car | $4,000–$7,500 |
| Full-service movers + drive car | $6,000–$12,000+ |
| Add vehicle shipping instead of driving | +$900–$2,300, minus ~$250–$350 fuel |

If you ship one car, one of you could fly, but then the dog's travel needs separate planning. Driving with the dog is usually simpler.

---

## Room-by-Room Packing Checklist

**Timeline:** non-essentials first, daily-use rooms last.
- **Weeks 6–4:** storage, garage, guest room, books, decor, off-season clothes
- **Weeks 3–2:** dining room, living room extras, office, most of the closets
- **Final week:** kitchen, bathroom, bedroom (leave essentials)

| Room | Pack | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Garage/storage** | Tools, seasonal items, sports gear | Movers won't take propane, paint, aerosols, fuel, or chemicals. Dispose of them locally. |
| **Guest room/decor** | Art (wrap it, box it flat), linens, lamps | Mark fragile items |
| **Office** | Files, electronics, cables | Photograph cable setups. Keep the laptop and important papers with you. |
| **Living room** | Books, media, small furniture | Disassemble furniture. Bag hardware and tape it to the piece. |
| **Kitchen** | Little-used appliances, extra dishes, pantry | Leave out 1 pot, 1 pan, plates, utensils, and a coffee setup |
| **Bathrooms** | Extra towels, backup toiletries | Seal liquids in zip bags |
| **Bedrooms** | Off-season clothes, extra bedding | Leave wardrobe boxes for last |
| **Closets** | Shoes, coats, bags | Donate what you haven't worn in a year |
| **Dog gear** | Extra beds, toys, supplies | Keep a go-bag separate (see below) |

**Declutter tips**
- Movers charge by weight, and every 1,000 lbs can add hundreds of dollars. Sell or donate first.
- Ask of each item: *Would I buy this again, and is it cheaper to replace than to move?* Cheap furniture and bulky items often are.
- Sell larger items on Facebook Marketplace or Craigslist 4–6 weeks out. Donate the rest and schedule pickups.
- Do one area per day. Don't try to purge the whole house in a weekend.
- Label boxes by room and priority: **Open First** or **Later**.
- Keep a **"Do Not Pack"** zone for items traveling with you, such as documents, medications, valuables, chargers, and the dog bag.

## Dog-Specific Checklist

**Now to 4 weeks out**
- [ ] **M** Vet visit: health check, rabies certificate, vaccine records, microchip number, and a medication refill covering the move plus a few weeks
- [ ] **M** Ask about car-sickness or anxiety medication, and test any medication before travel day
- [ ] **M** Check each hotel's pet policy (fees, weight limits, whether dogs can be left alone in the room)
- [ ] **M** Get a crash-tested crate or harness, and practice short drives

**1–2 weeks out**
- [ ] **M** Update ID tag with your cell number and the destination address
- [ ] **M** Plan a **July heat strategy**: drive early, break every 2–3 hours, never leave the dog in the car, and avoid hot pavement
- [ ] **M** Identify emergency vets along the route and in Oregon

**Moving day**
- [ ] **M** Dog stays in a quiet room, with a sitter, or at a friend's place while movers work
- [ ] **M** Walk and feed lightly before the drive to avoid car sickness

**Dog go-bag:** food for 5+ days, water jug, collapsible bowls, leash and spare leash, poop bags, medications, records, bed or blanket, favorite toy, chews, towel, wipes, and a recent photo of the dog on your phone

**After arrival:** update the microchip registry, get an Oregon dog license, book the first vet visit, and find the nearest 24-hour emergency vet.

## Cancel / Start Services Timeline

| Service | Action | When |
|---|---|---|
| Internet (Oregon) | Schedule install | **Now** |
| USPS | Change of address | 2 weeks before |
| Electric/gas/water (Ohio) | Schedule stop date | 3–4 weeks out, effective the day after you leave |
| Electric/gas/water (Oregon) | Schedule start | 3–4 weeks out, effective before arrival |
| Auto/renters/home insurance | Update or get new quotes | 2–3 weeks out |
| Banks and credit cards | Update address | 1–2 weeks out |
| Employer/payroll | Update address and tax withholding | 2–3 weeks out |
| Phone plan | Check coverage, update billing | 2 weeks out |
| Streaming and memberships | Cancel, pause, or transfer (gyms, etc.) | 2–4 weeks out |
| Subscriptions/deliveries | Update address (Amazon, meal kits, medications) | 1–2 weeks out |
| Doctors, dentists, pharmacy | Get records and transfer prescriptions | 3–4 weeks out |
| Ohio trash/cable | Cancel, return equipment | 1–2 weeks out |
| SSA, IRS, voter registration | Update address | After arrival |
| Oregon DMV | License and vehicle registration | Within 30 days of arrival (verify) |
| Renters insurance (Oregon) | Active on key day | Arrival |

## 8-Week Reminder Calendar

Assumes a **Thursday, July 16** move-out. Adjust if yours is different. Enter these as calendar events with alerts.

**Now to Week 9**
- **Thu May 7:** Give landlord written notice or call a realtor. Request 3+ mover quotes. Price DIY and container options.
- **Sat May 9:** Vet appointment request. Start the Moving folder (paper and digital).
- **Wed May 13:** Compare quotes, check USDOT numbers on FMCSA SAFER, and book the mover or truck.

**8 weeks out**
- **Thu May 21:** Book temporary housing and dog-friendly route lodging. Book vehicle shipping if applicable. Schedule internet install.

**7 weeks**
- **Thu May 28:** Start decluttering the garage, storage, and closets. Order a first batch of boxes. List large items for sale.

**6 weeks**
- **Thu Jun 4:** Check title or lienholder status. Research DEQ requirements for your Oregon address. Tell your employer your final dates.

**5 weeks**
- **Thu Jun 11:** Vet visit and records if not done. Book car maintenance. Start packing non-essential rooms.

**4 weeks**
- **Thu Jun 18:** Schedule Ohio utility shutoffs and Oregon starts. Confirm movers in writing. Send medical and prescription transfers.

**3 weeks**
- **Thu Jun 25:** Donation pickups. Update insurance. Cancel or transfer memberships. Order the dog ID tag.

**2 weeks**
- **Thu Jul 2:** Submit USPS change of address. Update banks and employer. Final mover and truck confirmation. *(Note: Fri Jul 3 is the holiday, so businesses may be closed.)*

**1 week**
- **Thu Jul 9:** Defrost the fridge. Pack the dog bag and car kit. Photograph valuables. Confirm vehicle shipper, hotels, and the Oregon vet appointment.

**Final days**
- **Wed Jul 15:** Final cleaning and walk-through photos. Fuel the car. Pack the Do Not Pack zone.
- **Thu Jul 16:** Move day.

## 🖨️ MOVING DAY ESSENTIALS (One Page)

**Carry in the car, not the truck.**

**DOCUMENTS (one folder)**
☐ IDs/passports ☐ Vehicle titles, registration, insurance ☐ Lease/closing docs (both homes) ☐ Mover contract, Bill of Lading, inventory ☐ Vehicle shipping receipt ☐ Dog records ☐ Medical records and prescriptions ☐ Birth/marriage certificates, SS cards ☐ Employer letter ☐ Hotel confirmations

**MONEY & TECH**
☐ Cards and some cash for tips ☐ Phone chargers and car chargers ☐ Laptop/tablet ☐ Power bank ☐ Offline maps downloaded

**DOG**
☐ Crate/harness ☐ Leash + spare ☐ Food (5+ days) ☐ Water jug + bowls ☐ Meds ☐ Poop bags ☐ Bed/blanket + toy ☐ Wipes/towel ☐ Vet records ☐ Updated ID tag

**PEOPLE**
☐ Medications (a week or more) ☐ Water and snacks ☐ Toiletries and a change of clothes ☐ Sunglasses, sunscreen ☐ Phone numbers on paper

**CAR EMERGENCY KIT**
☐ Jumper cables ☐ Spare tire and jack ☐ Flashlight ☐ First-aid kit ☐ Tire inflator ☐ Roadside assistance info ☐ Sunshade

**FIRST-NIGHT BOX (Open First)**
☐ Sheets, pillows, towels ☐ Shower curtain ☐ Toilet paper ☐ Basic tools ☐ Paper plates and utensils ☐ Coffee setup ☐ Cleaning supplies ☐ Trash bags ☐ Light bulbs

**BEFORE LEAVING THE HOUSE**
☐ Walk-through video of every room ☐ Windows/doors locked ☐ Thermostat set ☐ Meter photos ☐ Keys and remotes returned ☐ Lights off ☐ Read and sign the Bill of Lading ☐ Dog and people in the car ☐ Drive time and first stop set

**ON THE ROAD**
☐ Stop every 2–3 hrs ☐ Never leave the dog in the car ☐ Keep fuel above ¼ tank ☐ Save receipts and mileage ☐ Text mover/shipper contact when you arrive
